summary: A fiction excerpt from Book 14, part 45, set during a museum-like group outing where the narrator, Nikko, Marcella and Dave divide up a project and choose between a flowchart's options. The narrator sides with Nikko on the theme, and Nikko invites her to a rally, which she reluctantly considers. Later the narrator and Nikko talk privately at a corner table about Zip, the police, Wheeze, the Group, and her older brother Wilson.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, the narrator and Nikko split from Marcella and Dave, then talk privately about Zip, Wheeze, the Group and Wilson.
key_facts: Nikko makes an elaborate bow with his wool cap, speaking as if he were in a Shakespeare play, and asks Marcella to read on.
Nikko says he figured the narrator was involved with the flowchart's people, and the narrator replies that she does not know any of those people.
The group they are associated with has a website, a Facebook page, a Twitter account and a YouTube channel.
Nikko invites the narrator to a rally and offers to pick her up; she replies that she will ride her bike.
The narrator says Wilson went to rallies all the time and acted like he was doing something important, even though they never actually fixed anything.
Dave arrives late after giving an explanation about car problems and traffic, and Marcella hands him a flowchart.
The narrator votes for the second option, the one in green, and Nikko says he agrees.
Marcella orders everyone to assemble in the main lobby in exactly one hour to report.
Marcella asks Dave to follow her to the medieval art section, while Nikko and the narrator are assigned European and contemporary art.
The theme choices are 'communities' and 'animals'; the narrator and Nikko say the words at the same time, then swap them.
Dave says he will go along with whatever everybody else wants, and the narrator describes him as easygoing and agreeable so long as everyone else does the work.
The narrator tells Nikko about Zip, about police who came to the apartment and tried to throw their weight around, and about her worry over Wheeze.
The narrator nearly reveals what the Group uncovered about Zip's identity and an FBI agent he worked with, but she catches herself and presents it as her own research.
The narrator says she talked about Wilson, who took care of her when she was little, and that she wanted to go with him when he turned eighteen.
